name: Egress MITM proxy
tagline: A MITM HTTP/HTTPS proxy that implements split-brain DNS for egress traffic control in containerised environments. Decide per host where traffic goes, what gets through and which headers travel with it.

features.title: Split-brain DNS
features.body: via TCP dial interception, routing to target_ip or target_host

features.title: Path-based routing
features.body: different paths on one domain to different backends

features.title: ACL
features.body: whitelist, blacklist and passthrough with exact, wildcard and regex matching

features.title: Header policies
features.body: inject headers, strip sensitive ones, automatic X-Request-ID

features.title: Upstream TLS trust
features.body: custom PEM bundle or PKCS#12 truststore, per-target bypass

features.title: Hot reload
features.body: apply config changes with SIGHUP, no restart

features.title: Audit & tracing
features.body: JSON log of blocked requests, opt-in request traces with redaction

features.title: Operable
features.body: Prometheus metrics, health endpoints, graceful shutdown

sections.title: How a request flows
sections.intro: Your app keeps calling the real hostnames. The proxy decides at dial time — not in DNS — whether and where the connection goes.

steps.title: Intercept
steps.body: The app sends HTTP and HTTPS through the proxy. TLS is terminated with your own internal CA.

steps.title: Check the ACL
steps.body: Whitelist, blacklist or passthrough. Anything unmatched follows default_policy — BLOCK answers 403.

steps.title: Rewrite
steps.body: Route by domain and path to a target IP or host, change scheme or port, inject or drop headers.

steps.title: Forward
steps.body: Dial the real target over HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2, verified against your upstream CA bundle.

sections.title: Patterns that don't fail open
sections.intro: ACLs, rewrites and traces share one domain syntax. Matching is case-insensitive, trailing dots are stripped, and regex patterns are anchored — so a denylist entry can't be slipped past.

sections.title: Run it as a sidecar
sections.intro: Point your app at the proxy with the standard proxy variables. /healthz and /readyz plug into Kubernetes probes; on SIGTERM it fails readiness first, then drains in-flight requests.
sections.code:
env:
  - name: HTTPS_PROXY
    value: "http://localhost:8080"
  - name: HTTP_PROXY
    value: "http://localhost:8080"
sections.aside: Change rules without a restart: send SIGHUP and the config reloads.
